items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for House Speaker
items.feedTitle: Democrats formally nominate Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, paving way for him to be the first Black speaker
items.summary: House Democrats formally nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries to become Speaker, putting him on track to become the first Black American to lead the chamber when the new Congress convenes in January. Jeffries secured broad support from 251 lawmakers, though eleven Democrats voted against him, including a bloc of seven progressives. The nomination marks a historic moment for Democratic leadership and positions Jeffries as a prominent opposition voice against the Trump administration.

items.title: Trump to meet Putin separately during China visit
items.feedTitle: Trump plans to meet separately with Putin on his China trip in addition to their 3-way talks with Xi
items.summary: President Trump plans to hold a separate bilateral meeting with Russian President Putin during his trip to China, in addition to a scheduled three-way summit with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meetings underscore ongoing diplomatic engagement amid tensions over Ukraine and trade relations. A US official confirmed the arrangement as Trump prepares for high-stakes discussions on multiple fronts.

items.title: VP Vance cancels schedule to address tech outages
items.feedTitle: Vance scraps schedule to address tech outages as Trump admin insists incidents aren't linked
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance scrapped his scheduled commitments to hold crisis talks addressing a cascade of technology outages affecting government and private systems. The Trump administration has insisted the incidents—including disruptions to Microsoft, banking systems, and flights—are unrelated and not the result of a coordinated attack. Officials say system failures are due to unrelated technical issues and software updates.

items.title: Food aid rule disrupts early retirement plans
items.feedTitle: She retired early to care for family. New work rules for food aid disrupted that
items.summary: New Trump administration rules tightening SNAP food assistance have disrupted the retirement plans of older adults up to age 65, who now must work or volunteer to continue receiving benefits. The sweeping changes to work requirements mean many seniors who retired early to care for family members face difficult choices about re-entering the workforce. The policy shifts mark a significant tightening of eligibility criteria under the new administration.

items.title: Biden releases memoir on presidency and exit decision
items.feedTitle: Biden releases memoir recounting his presidency and decision to drop out in 2024
items.summary: Former President Joe Biden has published his memoir 'Promise Me, America,' recounting his time in the White House and his decision to withdraw from the 2024 presidential race. The book comes nearly two years after leaving office, though Biden is not conducting the typical media circuit to promote it. His former counselor Steve Ricchetti discussed the memoir's significance in reflecting on a transformative period.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport opens November 30
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: The MetroLink extension service to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport is set to begin operations on November 30, expanding regional transit connectivity. The project represents a major infrastructure advancement for the St. Louis metro area, linking the airport to the existing MetroLink system. The opening date was confirmed and announced by transit officials.

stlouis.title: Dollar General settles Missouri pricing case for $5.3M
stlouis.feedTitle: Dollar General to pay $5.3 million in Missouri pricing settlement
stlouis.summary: Dollar General has agreed to pay $5.3 million to resolve a Missouri pricing settlement, addressing consumer protection violations. The settlement stems from pricing practices that the state found problematic. The resolution represents a significant enforcement action by Missouri authorities against the major retailer.

stlouis.title: St. Louis launches voluntary home buyout flood program
stlouis.feedTitle: City of St. Louis CDA to Launch Voluntary Home Buyout Program for Flood Risk Mitigation
stlouis.summary: The City of St. Louis Community Development Agency is launching a voluntary home buyout program aimed at mitigating flood risk in vulnerable neighborhoods. The initiative offers eligible residents the opportunity to sell their properties to the city at fair-market value as part of a broader flood resilience strategy. The program represents efforts to address chronic flooding issues affecting city residents.

items.title: Trump is trying to put the Iran war behind him, but it’s not over
items.feedTitle: Trump is trying to put the Iran war behind him, but it’s not over
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza
items.feedTitle: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza, dozens flee
items.summary: Israeli forces have launched a new ground military operation in central Gaza, marking the first significant ground push since a ceasefire began. Dozens of Palestinians have fled the area as Israeli tanks rolled into the region west of the Yellow Line. The operation signals ongoing tensions despite ceasefire arrangements and raises concerns about civilian safety.

items.title: Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge with long-range weapons
items.feedTitle: ‘Crimea is turning into an island’: How Ukraine hit Putin’s prized bridge
items.summary: Ukraine conducted a weeks-long operation resulting in two waves of strikes on the Crimea Bridge using domestically-developed long-range missiles and drones. The strikes dealt a significant blow to Russian military infrastructure, with analysts noting that 'Crimea is turning into an island' as supply routes are cut. The operation represents Ukrainian success in asymmetric warfare against Russian positions.

items.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 globally
items.feedTitle: Muslims to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, study finds
items.summary: A new study projects that Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, marking a historic demographic shift in global religious populations. The Pew Research Center analysis examines population growth trends across the 2020–2070 period. This projection reflects differential birth rates and demographic patterns among the world's two largest religious groups.

items.title: Trump and Xi shake hands ahead of historic talks
items.feedTitle: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
items.summary: President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping shook hands in Shenzhen as the three leaders—including Russian President Putin—prepared for an unprecedented trilateral summit. The body language and diplomatic choreography of their greeting drew analysis from observers. The meeting represents a rare moment of direct engagement between the US and China at the highest levels amid significant strategic tensions.

items.title: Prince William and Kate reflect on UK-India ties with Modi
items.feedTitle: William and Kate reflect on 'enduring' UK-India ties with Modi
items.summary: Britain's Prince William and Princess Catherine met with Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi at the conclusion of their three-day India visit, discussing strengthening UK-India strategic partnership. The meeting highlighted the 'enduring' ties between the two nations and reinforced commitment to deeper cooperation. The royal visit included appearances at the annual Earthshot Prize and other high-profile events.

items.title: Delhi court orders charges in NEET paper leak case
items.feedTitle: NEET paper leak: Court orders charges against 14 accused
items.summary: A Delhi court has ordered charges to be framed against 14 accused persons in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak scandal. Day-to-day trial proceedings are set to begin on November 25, moving the case toward resolution. The charges represent a significant step in the investigation and prosecution of one of India's major recent exam integrity scandals.

items.title: India's October crude import bill soars 87.5% amid tensions
items.feedTitle: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
items.summary: India's crude oil import bill surged 87.5% to $19.5 billion in October compared to the previous year, driven by Middle East tensions and increased import volumes up 11%. The spike reflects higher global oil prices amid geopolitical uncertainty in the region. India's energy import costs have become a significant economic pressure point amid regional instability.

items.title: India imposes 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports
items.feedTitle: India imposes 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch imports amid UK trade pact dispute
items.summary: India has imposed a combined 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch whisky imports, escalating tensions over a pending UK trade pact dispute. The tariff reflects Indian protectionist measures amid ongoing negotiations with the UK over a comprehensive trade agreement. The move signals hardball negotiation tactics as both nations work toward finalizing trade terms.

items.title: India-US trade deal signing delayed pending tariff framework
items.feedTitle: India-US trade deal negotiations nearly finalised, signing delayed till new US tariff framework takes...
items.summary: India and the US have nearly finalized negotiations on a comprehensive trade deal, but the signing has been delayed pending clarity on the new US tariff framework under Trump administration policies. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal indicated that talks will wrap up soon, but formal signature depends on Washington establishing its tariff strategy. The delay reflects uncertainty about US trade policy direction.

immigration.title: DOL proposes major PERM green card overhaul (proposed, not final)
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The US Department of Labor has proposed sweeping changes to the PERM labor certification process—the first major overhaul in nearly 20 years—that would substantially tighten green card sponsorship rules for foreign workers. The proposed rule includes stricter recruitment requirements, extended job advertising periods, and enhanced labor market testing to prioritize US workers. This is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM); it is not yet finalized and is open for public comment.

immigration.title: H-1B visa issuances to Indians drop 88% in one month
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B visa issuances to Indians drop 88% in a single month as appointment crisis bites
immigration.summary: H-1B visa issuances to Indian nationals have plummeted 88% in a single month as a visa appointment processing crisis bites, with H-4 dependent visas falling 91%. The sharp decline reflects systemic delays at USCIS and reduced consular capacity, leaving many applicants unable to secure interview slots. The crisis underscores ongoing stress in the skilled immigration system under the Trump administration.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending H-1B USCIS deference rule (proposed, not final)
immigration.feedTitle: US government is proposing one sentence change in USCIS rules that would change every H-1B visa extension
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed eliminating the USCIS 'prior approval deference' rule that currently allows H-1B visa extensions for the same employer to proceed without full re-evaluation. The proposed change would subject roughly 208,000 work visa renewals annually to stricter checks, potentially triggering thousands of additional Requests for Evidence (RFEs). This is a proposed rule; comments closed November 13 and it has not yet been finalized.

items.title: Nvidia doubles revenue after Jensen Huang's exit
items.feedTitle: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia reported that revenue has doubled in its latest quarter as the company issued its first earnings report following Jensen Huang's exit as CEO. Board chairman Harvey Jones confirmed the company 'does not intend to reinstate' Huang, signaling a full transition to new leadership. The strong earnings and guidance underscore continued demand for AI chips, though leadership uncertainty remains a concern for investors.

items.title: Goldman Sachs upgrades India to overweight, sets 28,500 target
items.feedTitle: Goldman Sachs upgrades India to overweight, sets Nifty target of 28,500
items.summary: Goldman Sachs has upgraded India to overweight positioning and set a Nifty target of 28,500, signaling increased bullishness on Indian equities. The upgrade reflects improving economic fundamentals and market opportunities in the region. The price target represents significant upside from current levels and reflects confidence in India's growth trajectory.

items.title: Foreign portfolio inflows reach record $1.06 trillion in November
items.feedTitle: FPI stock-buying tops ₹1 trillion in November, highest-ever monthly inflow
items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have net purchased ₹1.06 lakh crore ($12.7 billion) worth of Indian stocks in November, marking the highest monthly FPI inflow ever recorded in India per NSDL data. In a single month, foreign investors reversed the combined ₹70,000 crore ($8.4 billion) outflow from September and October. The sharp reversal signals renewed confidence in Indian equities after a period of selling pressure.

items.title: Stock markets snap 2-day rally amid profit-booking, Fed fears
items.feedTitle: Stock markets snap 2-day rally; Sensex drops 500 points amid profit booking, U.S. Fed rate hike fears
items.summary: Indian stock markets ended a two-day winning streak as the Sensex fell 500 points and profit-booking dominated trading. Weakness was driven by concerns about US Federal Reserve rate hike prospects and broader market volatility. The decline follows a period of gains and reflects uncertainty about monetary policy direction and global economic conditions.

items.title: Tech outages blamed on rush to fix AI-detected bugs
items.feedTitle: ‘Zero’ evidence that recent cascade of tech outages are linked, says Rubio
items.summary: Recent cascading technology outages across the US—affecting flights, banks, and Apple services—have been attributed to a surge in software patches rushed out to fix vulnerabilities discovered by AI systems. Financial Times reporting suggests the rush to patch AI-found bugs may have contributed to systemic failures. The incidents highlight tensions between rapid AI-driven security updates and system stability risks.

finance.note: Oil prices have come under pressure amid broader tech outages affecting market sentiment, with crude sliding amid macroeconomic uncertainty. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq have fluctuated following mixed earnings—Nvidia's strong revenue beat offset by leadership transition concerns, while Anthropic's IPO pricing signals continued investor appetite for AI despite broader equity volatility. Watch: Anthropic's first-day trading performance and any shift in AI sector momentum; Fed speakers' commentary on rate trajectory given job market resilience; resolution of tech outage root causes and their systemic implications.

cards.title: Visa processing delays are eroding savings plans
cards.insight: H-1B and green card delays mean foreign workers are trapped in extended visa limbo, unable to plan salary transitions or relocations. Processing backlogs at USCIS are turning approved cases into administrative purgatory.
cards.takeaway: If you're on a work visa, build 6–12 months of additional emergency reserves to absorb delays and pivot costs; don't assume approved timelines.

cards.title: Tariff uncertainty is freezing hiring and wage negotiation
cards.insight: Companies facing proposed PERM rule changes and uncertain tariff frameworks are delaying hiring and salary decisions. Employer-sponsored green card sponsorship is becoming riskier, reducing worker leverage.
cards.takeaway: Lock in raises and job offers now before Q1 budget freezes hit; negotiate severance and equity vesting upfront if green card sponsorship is part of your package.

cards.title: Tech outages expose fragility in your financial access
cards.insight: Cascading bank, payment, and cloud system failures mean your money can become temporarily inaccessible despite nothing being wrong with your account. Single points of failure in patching cycles create systemic risk.
cards.takeaway: Keep 1–2 weeks of cash outside digital banking; verify multi-bank diversification and test withdrawal access from at least two institutions monthly.

cards.title: AI-driven chip restrictions are reshaping tech sector volatility
cards.insight: Nvidia's leadership transition and China export caps create uncertainty in semiconductor supply and pricing. AI infrastructure costs remain unpredictable, inflating cloud and software budgets.
cards.takeaway: Review cloud contracts for cost escalation clauses; consider locking in long-term pricing for critical SaaS tools now before AI-driven demand inflation accelerates further.

ai.title: Anthropic finalizes pricing for blockbuster IPO debut
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic Is Set to Finalize Pricing for Blockbuster I.P.O.
ai.summary: Anthropic is set to finalize pricing for its highly-anticipated initial public offering, which is expected to value the AI company at approximately $1.4 trillion. The IPO represents the largest AI company debut and follows massive institutional investor demand. The valuation reflects the company's rapid growth in revenue and market prominence as a leading Claude AI developer.

ai.title: Dario Amodei and Anthropic poised for billion-dollar wealth creation
ai.feedTitle: One of AI's most notorious 'doomers' stands to make billions in Anthropic's IPO
ai.summary: One of AI's most prominent 'doomers' and safety advocates, Dario Amodei and his team at Anthropic stand to become multi-billionaires following the company's IPO. The seven co-founders will see their stakes significantly appreciated, though the company remains heavily focused on AI safety research. The wealth creation underscores how AI safety has become a commercially attractive business proposition.

ai.title: US blocks Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing AI chips
ai.feedTitle: US blocks Chinese AI firms and 'other restricted entities' from remotely accessing American AI chips
ai.summary: The Trump administration has imposed new restrictions preventing Chinese AI firms and 'other restricted entities' from remotely accessing American artificial intelligence chips. The measure tightens existing export controls on advanced semiconductor technology to China. The policy reflects ongoing US efforts to constrain China's AI development capabilities through technology access restrictions.

ai.title: China-linked hackers using AI model ARTEX to infiltrate banks
ai.feedTitle: China-linked hackers using AI model ARTEX to infiltrate banks, FBI warns
ai.summary: The FBI has warned that China-linked hackers are using an AI model called ARTEX to infiltrate and compromise US banking institutions. The warning highlights how AI tools are being weaponized for sophisticated cyber-attacks against critical financial infrastructure. The threat represents a convergence of AI advancement and state-sponsored cyber espionage targeting the US financial system.

ai.title: OpenAI advances chip design with AI models
ai.feedTitle: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
ai.summary: OpenAI has announced progress in advancing semiconductor chip design using its AI models, demonstrating AI's application in improving hardware engineering. The work represents a convergence of AI development and chip manufacturing, potentially creating feedback loops that accelerate hardware progress. The capability highlights how frontier AI is being deployed to solve foundational technology challenges.
